lead: >-
  Margarita Island makes an ideal beach finale to a longer journey through Venezuela: after the boats and tropical forests of Canaima, you can spend several days beside the Caribbean Sea. But current Ada Tours itineraries offer different kinds of relaxation. One includes a guided island excursion visiting fortresses and towns, another focuses on a seaside hotel and optional activities, while a third adds Los Roques and the Orinoco Delta. Compare their daily programs and conditions to find the right route.
---

## Which Tours Include Margarita Island?

In our catalog you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} in which [Margarita Island](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/) forms part of **the main itinerary**, rather than being offered only as an optional post-tour excursion. All current options last 12 days and combine the island with [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/) and [Canaima National Park](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/). They differ in additional destinations and how the final days are spent.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_populyarnye_napravleniya_venesuely,tour_source_venesuela_prirodnye_kontrasty_tropikov,tour_source_luchshee_v_venesuele}}

| Itinerary | What Makes Its Margarita Stay Different |
|---|---|
| [Popular Destinations of Venezuela](/venezuela/tour/popular-destinations-of-venezuela/) | Relaxation and an included island sightseeing tour |
| [Best of Venezuela: Margarita](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/) | Several days in a seaside hotel, sightseeing by choice |
| [Natural Contrasts and Beaches](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/) | Margarita after Los Roques and the Orinoco |

**The same total trip duration does not mean the same amount of beach time.** Compare the dates of the island stay, number of sightseeing days, and onward transfers in each tour's published itinerary.

## Three Options: Beaches, History, or a Nature Journey

### “Popular Destinations of Venezuela”: An Island Tour Included

On the [“Popular Destinations of Venezuela” tour](/venezuela/tour/popular-destinations-of-venezuela/), the Margarita Island portion begins on day seven. After Canaima, flights via Caracas, a transfer, and check-in at a 4-star all-inclusive hotel are scheduled. Day eight is dedicated to beach relaxation.

On day nine, travelers enjoy **a sightseeing excursion with a Russian-speaking guide**. The route includes Juan Griego, La Galera Fort, the Pueblo de Margarita museum of traditional life, La Asunción, the Basilica of Our Lady of El Valle, and San Carlos de Borromeo Fortress in Pampatar. The itinerary also specifies lunch featuring local fish dishes and a drive along the coast. This option suits travelers interested in the island's history as well as its beaches.

Days ten and eleven are free for the sea again. The last day includes a flight to Caracas and a visit to the Santa Teresa estate. Check the [tour description](/venezuela/tour/popular-destinations-of-venezuela/) for exact services and daily arrangements rather than assuming they apply to other offers.

### “Best of Venezuela”: More Time for Independent Relaxation

On the [12-day tour featuring a beach stay on Margarita](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/), arrival on the island is also scheduled for day seven, after Canaima National Park. The program includes a transfer to Sunsol Ecoland and all-inclusive accommodation. Days 8–11 are devoted to relaxing beside the sea.

An island sightseeing excursion is **offered as an optional extra**. This is a significant difference from “Popular Destinations”: you can spend more time at the hotel and on the beach, but the sightseeing excursion should not be treated as part of the base package.

The current itinerary names a specific hotel. Confirm final accommodation conditions when choosing your trip: Ada Tours' published terms allow a hotel to be replaced with another of a comparable category. A name in the itinerary does not guarantee that the exact room or building will remain unchanged.

### “Natural Contrasts”: Los Roques and the Orinoco Too

The [“Natural Contrasts of Venezuela” tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/) has a more varied first section. Travelers begin on the [Los Roques archipelago](/venezuela/place/los-roques/), then visit [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) and the [Orinoco Delta](/venezuela/place/orinoco-delta/). They fly to Margarita on day nine; days ten and eleven are for the sea and all-inclusive hotel relaxation.

The published itinerary does not list a mandatory excursion devoted to Margarita's forts and towns. Do not automatically add one by analogy with another tour. The program alternates the Caribbean Sea, waterfalls, river excursions, and island relaxation.

For those who primarily want nature and marine scenery, the journey includes different coastal experiences: the small coral islands of Los Roques at the beginning and the more developed resort island of Margarita at the end.

## What Kind of Island Vacation Can You Expect on Margarita?

[Margarita](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/) lies in the Caribbean Sea and belongs to Nueva Esparta State. It has long sandy beaches, coastal settlements, waterfront promenades, and historic fortresses. Unlike the small islands of [Los Roques](/venezuela/place/los-roques/), Margarita allows visitors to combine hotel relaxation with road excursions around the island.

Conditions vary from beach to beach. Playa El Agua and Playa Parguito are known for long stretches of coastline and surf, while El Yaque is known for wind-based watersports. Mentioning these names in a guide, however, **does not make visiting every beach an obligatory part of the selected tour**. The particular beach, swimming conditions, and transfer time depend on accommodation, weather, and the actual daily itinerary.

For an unhurried stay, look beyond the number of nights to the hotel's location. A traveler primarily interested in beaches may prefer the option with four free days. Those eager to explore historic quarters and fortresses should choose an itinerary where the relevant sightseeing excursion is included in the main program.

## What Is There on the Island Beyond the Beaches?

### Fortresses and Towns

[Margarita Island](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/) has a rich colonial heritage. San Carlos de Borromeo Fortress near Pampatar, La Galera Fort in Juan Griego, and central La Asunción reveal another side of the island. These sites can be combined on a sightseeing trip, but they are **included in “Popular Destinations of Venezuela”**, not automatically in every tour in the catalog.

The included sightseeing excursion also visits the Basilica of Our Lady of El Valle, a religious site important to local residents. Pueblo de Margarita introduces visitors to traditional houses and crafts. This kind of day fits well between several beach days.

### Lagoons, Mangroves, and Natural Areas

One of the island's best-known protected natural sites is La Restinga Lagoon, with mangroves and shallow waters. It has conservation importance and is listed among Ramsar wetlands. It is a separate destination for travelers interested in Venezuelan nature.

However, **none of the three tours being compared should be advertised as including a mandatory La Restinga excursion** unless the visit is explicitly scheduled in its daily itinerary. For the natural experiences actually listed, look at [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) and, on the relevant tour, the [Orinoco](/venezuela/place/orinoco-delta/).

## Margarita vs. Los Roques: What Is Different for Your Itinerary?

| Criterion | Los Roques | Margarita |
|---|---|---|
| Main Type of Holiday | Small islands, reefs | Beaches, resorts, towns |
| Typical Excursions | Boats and marine outings | Beaches and road trips around the island |
| On Ada Tours Journeys | Beginning of two itineraries | End of three itineraries |

[Los Roques](/venezuela/place/los-roques/) is ideal for travelers seeking white-sand islets and clear waters over reefs. [Margarita](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/) is better suited to several days in a hotel, beach relaxation, and road trips to towns and fortresses. Your choice depends on whether you want more time at sea or wish to vary your vacation with history and sightseeing.

Both destinations can be combined: [“Natural Contrasts of Venezuela”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/) includes the archipelago and Margarita. The other current tours in this selection emphasize Margarita without promising an obligatory Los Roques stop.

## Practical Tips for Choosing a Margarita Tour

First, check **the day of the flight to the island and the day of departure**. Two programs arrive on day seven, while the third arrives on day nine. This affects actual beach time more than the shared “12 days” label.

Second, compare what excursions are included. On [“Popular Destinations”](/venezuela/tour/popular-destinations-of-venezuela/), the island tour is part of the main itinerary. On [“Best of Venezuela”](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/), it is optional. On [“Natural Contrasts”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/), the island portion is described as a hotel stay and relaxation.

Third, consider the earlier days. [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) features boats, excursions, and walking on certain days. A few quiet days on Margarita may therefore be particularly welcome. If a wider range of nature is the priority, the [Orinoco Delta](/venezuela/place/orinoco-delta/) adds forested rivers and wildlife observation.

Also explore [all Venezuela tours](/venezuela/tour/) and [beach holidays in Venezuela](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/venezuela/). Each itinerary has its own accommodation, flight, guide, and excursion terms. They should not be generalized across all three routes.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Margarita Island Tours

### How Many Days Are Spent on Margarita?

On [“Popular Destinations of Venezuela”](/venezuela/tour/popular-destinations-of-venezuela/) and [“Best of Venezuela”](/venezuela/tour/best-of-venezuela-margarita-island-12-days/), the island stay begins on day seven. On [“Natural Contrasts”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/), it begins on day nine. Part of the final day is used for departure or flying, so calendar days are not the same as completely free beach days.

### Is There a Tour with an Included Island Excursion?

Yes. [“Popular Destinations of Venezuela”](/venezuela/tour/popular-destinations-of-venezuela/) includes a day-nine excursion with a Russian-speaking guide, towns, fortresses, and cultural stops. Another 12-day option offers sightseeing at the traveler's choice.

### Are All-Inclusive Meals Included?

The Margarita accommodation on all three current itineraries is described as **all-inclusive**. The exact package, restrictions, and hotel conditions must nonetheless be taken from the chosen tour. Do not apply one itinerary's hotel or drinks selection to another.

### Can I Combine Margarita and Angel Falls?

Yes. All three tours covered here visit [Canaima National Park and Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) before the beach portion. The waterfall is in another region of Venezuela and requires a separate travel stage and internal logistics.

### Is There a Route Including Both Margarita and Los Roques?

Yes. The [12-day “Natural Contrasts of Venezuela” tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-tropical-contrasts-beaches-12-days/) includes [Los Roques](/venezuela/place/los-roques/) at the start and [Margarita](/venezuela/place/margarita-island/) at the end. Canaima and the Orinoco lie between them.

## Mérida in Venezuela: A City at the Foot of the Andes

Mérida lies in western [Venezuela](/venezuela/), surrounded by the Andes. It is a major university and cultural center, with streets, squares, markets, and quick access to mountain scenery. A visit can combine exploring the historic city with separate excursions to the highlands.

Venezuela's Mérida should not be confused with the city of the same name in Mexico. This page concerns **Mérida in the Andes**, whose principal natural landmarks include the Sierra Nevada range, high-altitude lakes, and the Mukumbarí cable car.

In Mérida itself, visitors can see the university, the old La Parroquia quarter, churches, markets, and nearby attractions. This lends itself to two distinct aspects of a journey: city sightseeing and mountain excursions.

## The Mukumbarí Cable Car

One of the city's best-known attractions is the Mukumbarí cable car system, climbing high into the Andes. Its upper station at Pico Espejo lies several thousand meters above sea level, and the journey offers a transition from urban scenery to cold high-altitude terrain.

The cable car periodically closes for maintenance, so **the fact that the attraction is in the city does not confirm an ascent on your tour date**. Venezuela's tourism ministry reported that the system reopened on August 19, 2026 after maintenance. This confirms that the facility operated in 2026, but its current schedule and accessible sections should be checked immediately before visiting.

The altitude and winds may affect operation. Travelers should prepare for low temperatures at the top, weather restrictions, and their own response to altitude. A jacket, closed-toe footwear, and sun protection are needed even when the city itself is warm.

## Historic Center, University, and Markets

Mérida is known for student life and cultural traditions. Its urban attractions include the historic La Parroquia district, central streets, churches, squares, and outdoor markets. Notable places include the church at Plaza Rangel del Llano and the Mercado Principal market.

A city walk offers an introduction to the crafts, cuisine, and everyday life of the Venezuelan Andes. It differs from an excursion to high-altitude lakes: there is no lengthy acclimatization to extreme altitude, and the itinerary can usually cover several city blocks.

When selecting an excursion, ask whether the market or a particular museum is included or whether you would visit during free time. Do not assume that every urban attraction is included simply because several are within walking distance.

## Nature Around Mérida

### Sierra Nevada and High-Altitude Landscapes

The mountainous areas of Sierra Nevada National Park lie near Mérida. They feature the characteristic Andean páramo landscapes: open highland terrain with specialized vegetation, rocky slopes, and cold lakes.

Trips here require a different approach from city walks. Even a short stop above the clouds may be cold and windy, and long treks are not suitable for every traveler.

### Mountain Lakes and Rural Villages

The area around Mérida offers mountain villages and lakes, including [Mucubají Lagoon](/venezuela/place/mucubaji-lagoon/) if it is explicitly on your itinerary. Visiting a high-altitude lake differs from riding the cable car, requiring ground transportation and separate travel time.

When planning, it is better to choose one main natural area for a day than attempt to combine distant sections of the Andes into a short excursion.

## When to Visit and How to Prepare

Climate changes with altitude: temperatures are generally milder in the city and significantly colder on the upper cable car stations and mountain passes. Rainfall and cloud cover can reduce visibility. Ideal weather for city sightseeing does not guarantee good views from the cable car.

For high-altitude outings, bring warm layers, sunglasses, and water. Rapid ascent of several thousand meters makes individual tolerance of altitude important; you should also be able to stop ascending if you feel unwell.

If planning a journey through [Venezuela](/venezuela/), compare Mérida with the plains of [Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/) and the beaches of [Los Roques](/venezuela/place/los-roques/). They offer three completely different experiences: mountains and culture, wildlife-filled savanna, and the Caribbean Sea.

## Adding Mérida to an Ada Tours Itinerary

Mérida works well as a dedicated section of a Venezuela itinerary, with city walks, the cable car, and mountain outings. Exact inclusions depend on the tour: cable car operation may be restricted, while some natural excursions require extra transport and time.

On the [Venezuela tours page](/venezuela/tour/), compare the days, included sights, and arrangements. If mountain scenery and long walks appeal to you, also explore our [adventure journeys](/interests/adventure/), but do not equate any cable car ride with a mountain trek.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Mérida

### Is Mérida in Venezuela or Mexico?

Both countries have cities named Mérida. Here we mean **Mérida in Venezuela**, located in the Andes in Mérida State.

### Is the Mukumbarí Cable Car Operating?

It reopened after maintenance in 2026. Its current schedule, weather restrictions, and access to upper stations must be confirmed shortly before visiting.

### Which Natural Places Are Near Mérida?

The mountain landscapes of Sierra Nevada National Park, high-altitude lakes including [Mucubají](/venezuela/place/mucubaji-lagoon/), and picturesque Andean valleys.

### Can Mérida and Los Roques Be Combined?

In principle, they can be part of a longer Venezuela journey, but they are distant and very different regions. Domestic travel arrangements and the number of days must be planned separately.

## Which Current Tours Pass Through Mérida?

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring [Mérida](/venezuela/place/merida/) on the main itinerary. This is the city in Mérida State, western Venezuela, near the Venezuelan Andes. Both journeys last 12 days and connect the country's western regions with [Canaima and Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), but allocate their days very differently.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_venesuela_novye_konkistadory,tour_source_krasota_venesuely}}

| Tour | Mérida's Role |
|---|---|
| [“New Conquistadors”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/) | A city-center walk after the páramo |
| [Venezuela Nature and Beaches](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/) | Arrival point and onward travel |

This distinction is essential. **The presence of Mérida in a list of places does not guarantee a cable car ride, an extensive city tour, or a separate day for sightseeing.** Open the daily itinerary to see what happens after arrival.

## “New Conquistadors”: The Andes, Páramo, and a Walk in Mérida

The [“Venezuela — New Conquistadors” tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/) begins at [Choroní](/venezuela/place/choroni/) on the Caribbean coast. It continues with [Canaima and Salto Ángel](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) and wildlife viewing in [Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/). The Andean section takes place in the final days.

On day ten, travelers head into the highlands. The itinerary includes the Capilla de Piedras stone-chapel monument and a walk from [Mucubají Lagoon](/venezuela/place/mucubaji-lagoon/) to Laguna Negra. Part of the trail may offer mule rental, payable locally. This is a genuine mountain section requiring appropriate footwear, attention to temperature, and enough time for the walk.

Day eleven combines thermal springs, páramo landscapes, and Mérida. Along the way, named stops include the Mifafí station with Andean condors, mountain villages, and Mucuchíes. The group then takes **a walk through central Mérida**, including Simón Bolívar Square, the cathedral, and urban neighborhoods. The program also mentions a local ice cream shop with unusual flavors. An overnight stay in the city follows.

Day twelve includes a transfer to the airport and a flight to [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/). Mérida therefore forms part of an eventful final sequence of mountain sights, although there is little spare time for independent exploration of the city.

### The Cable Car Is an Optional Activity on This Tour

On “New Conquistadors,” Mukumbarí is described as **an optional visit by choice**, with the ticket paid for on site. Other optional attractions include the botanical garden, an Andean market, and a toy museum. None should be presented as a guaranteed inclusion in the main day.

The Mukumbarí cable car connects the city to high-altitude stations in Sierra Nevada National Park. Its upper Pico Espejo station lies around 4,765 m above sea level. Conditions here differ markedly from a city-center stroll: temperatures may be low, winds strong, and visibility change quickly.

Cable car operations may be suspended for maintenance or weather. Even if the infrastructure is generally operating, the specific date, ticket, and ascent to the top station require separate confirmation. **Do not book on the assumption of a mandatory ascent** unless it is a confirmed inclusion.

## “Nature and Beaches”: Mérida as a Transport Stop

On the [12-day nature-and-beaches journey](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/), the opening days are spent on the coast at [Choroní](/venezuela/place/choroni/), followed by [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/). Day seven features a flight from Canaima via Caracas to Mérida and a transfer to a hotel.

This confirms a visit to the city, but **day seven is described as a travel day**, without a separate Mérida sightseeing excursion. On day eight, travelers already head toward [Lake Maracaibo](/venezuela/place/lake-maracaibo/) and the Catatumbo lightning area. The route later continues through [La Azulita](/venezuela/place/la-azulita/) and mountain districts toward [Barinas](/venezuela/place/barinas/), followed by nature trips in [Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/).

The western part of this itinerary is primarily about nature and changes in landscape: lake, river and mountain roads, and savanna. Mérida is important for logistics, but the published description does not include a full day of city sightseeing.

If your goal is Mérida's architecture, cable car, and several independent city walks, this option should not be selected simply because the city appears on the route. Catatumbo and savanna wildlife are more characteristic of this journey.

## What Is Interesting in and Around Mérida?

[Mérida](/venezuela/place/merida/) stands near the ranges of the Venezuelan Andes. Its historic center, university neighborhoods, cathedral, markets, and squares are surrounded by valleys, cloud forests, and high-altitude páramo vegetation. Unlike Venezuela's beach regions, the climate here varies significantly with elevation.

### A Walk Around the City

Plaza Bolívar, the cathedral, old streets, and local markets are sensible choices for a short introduction. On “New Conquistadors,” this walk is included on day eleven. It provides a glimpse of the city after several natural regions, but it is not the equivalent of a multi-day city tour.

For churches, the university, and Mérida's neighborhoods in greater detail, consult the separate [city guide](/venezuela/place/merida/). This catalog page has a narrower purpose: it explains **which tours actually visit Mérida and what is included during the stay**.

### High-Altitude Lagoons and Páramo

On [“New Conquistadors”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/), day ten includes [Mucubají Lagoon](/venezuela/place/mucubaji-lagoon/) and a hike around Laguna Negra. Tropical vegetation gives way to grassy slopes, mosses, and characteristic high-altitude plants. The route passes through high terrain, so physical effort feels different from that at sea level.

In the Andes, leave time for slower movement, changing weather, and suitable clothing. The actual effort depends on the length of the walk and each participant's condition. The possibility of riding a mule on one section does not imply that all mountain walks can be replaced by transport.

### Mukumbarí and Sierra Nevada

The Mukumbarí system consists of several stations climbing from the city of Mérida into the highlands. Venezuela's tourism authorities place its highest point at approximately 4,765 m. Temperature, wind, and how travelers feel can change sharply with altitude, so it is best to plan the trip separately from an ordinary city walk.

On the [“New Conquistadors” tour](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/), the cable car is one of the optional activities, not an included excursion. On the second program, it is not mentioned at all as part of the Mérida day. **The region's best-known attraction is not necessarily included on a commercial itinerary.**

## How to Choose Between the Two Journeys

For travelers who want both the city and the páramo, [“New Conquistadors”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/) is the better match. Its daily program explicitly mentions high-altitude lagoons, driving through mountain villages, hot springs, and a walk in Mérida. The cable car remains optional even here.

If your priority is observing natural phenomena and animals, choose the [route through Maracaibo and Los Llanos](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/). It links the beaches, [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), [Lake Maracaibo](/venezuela/place/lake-maracaibo/), [La Azulita](/venezuela/place/la-azulita/), and the savannas. Mérida serves as a transport connection between regions.

| Your Priority | More Suitable Option |
|---|---|
| Mérida city and páramo | “New Conquistadors” |
| Lake Maracaibo and Catatumbo | “Nature and Beaches” |
| Wildlife observation | Both tours |
| Cable car included | Neither is confirmed to include it |

The journeys share several destinations, most notably [Canaima](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/) and [Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/). Shared regional names do not guarantee the same activities, accommodation, or guiding. Compare the wider geography in the [Venezuela tours catalog](/venezuela/tour/) and the specific terms of each tour.

## What to Prepare for in the Venezuelan Andes

For the mountain portion, the key considerations are altitude, weather, and travel time. Even when it is warm below, the páramo lagoons and upper cable car stations may require warm layers and wind protection. Comfortable boots are useful on damp, rocky paths; water and sun protection matter on open terrain.

If you begin on the [Choroní coast](/venezuela/place/choroni/) and later travel through the highlands, the shift between climate zones happens within a single journey. Anyone sensitive to altitude or planning active walks should prepare for the elevation and discuss it with a doctor if they have relevant medical concerns.

**Do not plan an additional sightseeing day based only on the promotional name “Mérida.”** “New Conquistadors” already has a full mountain program, while the [Catatumbo itinerary](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/) makes only a short city stop. A separate Mukumbarí ascent or extra time for walks requires a specific itinerary change and agreed logistics.

National parks and tourism infrastructure may also have seasonal restrictions. Cable car operations, mountain weather, and domestic flight schedules should be checked for the dates of travel. A published sequence of days is useful for understanding the route, but cannot replace confirmed tickets.

## Experiences to Combine with Mérida

Western Venezuela offers opportunities to combine distinct natural regions. [Mucubají Lagoon](/venezuela/place/mucubaji-lagoon/) is a high-altitude landscape, [Lake Maracaibo](/venezuela/place/lake-maracaibo/) is associated with lowland waters and the Catatumbo phenomenon, while [Los Llanos](/venezuela/place/los-llanos/) features savannas and wildlife.

These destinations require different amounts of time and means of transport. One day in Mérida is not enough to explore the city center, all the high-altitude lagoons, and distant natural areas in depth. For [nature tours in Venezuela](/interests/wildlife/tours/venezuela/), assess the sequence of regions and leave enough time for travel.

If you are planning a more active journey, explore [adventure tours in Venezuela](/interests/adventure/tours/venezuela/). The actual activity level is determined by the itinerary; mountain scenery alone does not imply strenuous trekking.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Tours Through Mérida

### Which Tour Includes Mérida City Sightseeing?

On [“New Conquistadors”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/), day eleven includes a walk through the center, Simón Bolívar Square, and the cathedral. On the [Lake Maracaibo route](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-nature-beaches-12-days/), Mérida is the arrival and overnight point before the next stage; its day-seven description does not include a separate city excursion.

### Is the Mukumbarí Cable Car Included in the Price?

A mandatory Mukumbarí visit is not confirmed in either tour. On “New Conquistadors,” it is an optional activity with the ticket paid on site. Opening hours and accessibility must be checked separately.

### Can I Visit Mucubají Lagoon?

Yes. [“New Conquistadors”](/venezuela/tour/venezuela-new-conquistadors/) includes [Mucubají Lagoon](/venezuela/place/mucubaji-lagoon/) and a walk in the Laguna Negra area. This is part of a mountain day before reaching Mérida. The second itinerary does not specify it as a mandatory stop.

### Can Mérida and Canaima Be Combined?

Yes. Both current Mérida itineraries also include [Canaima and Angel Falls](/venezuela/place/canaima-and-angel-falls/), although the visits take place on different days and require domestic flights or road transfers. The attractions are in different regions of Venezuela.

## Mount Roraima in Venezuela: Trekking to the Summit of a Tepui

**Mount Roraima (Monte Roraima)** is one of South America's best-known table mountains. Its nearly level plateau rises above the savanna on sheer rock walls. The mountain sits at the border of [Venezuela](/venezuela/), Brazil, and Guyana; tourist treks usually approach from the Venezuelan side.

Roraima is one of the **tepuis**, ancient table mountains of the Guiana Highlands. Many of their summits were isolated from the surrounding lowlands for long geological periods. Consequently, the plateau landscape differs dramatically from the open savanna below.

## Why Is Roraima Called the Lost World?

From below, you see an immense rocky massif whose top frequently disappears into clouds. The plateau contains stone labyrinths, small natural pools, stretches of quartz-rich rock, and unusual plants adapted to poor soils and constant moisture.

The image of a “lost world” reflects the atmosphere of high, isolated plateaus and literary associations with Arthur Conan Doyle's novel. It is a figurative name, not a claim that unknown large animals live on the mountain.

According to Venezuela's national parks institute, Roraima stands approximately **2,810 m** above sea level. Yet the difficulty of the trek depends on more than summit altitude: the route is long, gains elevation, includes river crossings, and is exposed to changeable weather.

## The Journey from Savanna to Plateau

The normal route does not begin on the mountain itself. Travelers first head across Gran Sabana toward settlements near [San Francisco de Yuruani](/venezuela/place/san-francisco-de-yuruani/) and Paraitepui, where the hiking section starts.

Over the multi-day trek, the landscape changes in stages:

- **Savanna.** Open grasslands, initial views of the tepui walls, and long days on foot.
- **Rivers and the Mountain's Base.** Rocky fords, fluctuating water levels, and increasingly damp ground.
- **Rocky Ascent.** A steep section alongside cliffs, with stones, roots, and sometimes slippery surfaces.
- **Plateau.** Unusual stone formations, mist, small pools, and different kinds of quartz terrain.

The weather can affect the pace and accessibility of certain sections. Reaching the summit requires prepared guiding arrangements and compliance with national park rules.

## What to See on the Summit

The upper plateau is known for rock shapes carved by water and wind over long periods. Quartz crystals are common, along with sandstone formations resembling animals or fantastical sculptures.

Small natural pools are sometimes called “Roraima's Jacuzzis.” They are natural depressions in the rock filled with water, not equipped bathing facilities. Guides and conservation regulations determine whether approaching or swimming in them is allowed.

The plants include species adapted to nutrient-poor soils, including endemic forms. Collecting crystals, plants, or stones is prohibited: Roraima lies within the protected territory of Canaima National Park.

## Do You Need to Be Physically Fit?

A Roraima hike is **a multi-day trek**, not a short ascent to a viewpoint. Although the plateau is lower than many Andean summits, travelers cover considerable distances carrying backpacks, sometimes in cold and rainy weather.

Proper trekking boots, waterproof clothing, a warm layer, protection for gear against rain, and readiness to spend several days on the route are important. The actual itinerary depends on trek duration, group size, river crossing conditions, and permits for the protected area.

Local guides, including members of the Pemón community, know the trails, weather patterns, and visiting rules. Organizing the journey should acknowledge their role and the national park's current requirements.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Mount Roraima

### Is Roraima Entirely in Venezuela?

No. The mountain stands near the Venezuela–Brazil–Guyana border, although tourist trekking routes usually approach from Venezuela.

### How High Is Roraima?

Approximately 2,810 m above sea level, according to Canaima National Park information.

### Can You Reach the Summit in One Day?

Not by the normal trekking route. The ascent and return take several days and require preparation.

### What Is Special About the Plateau?

Quartz-rich rock, unusual stone formations, mist, and plants adapted to an isolated high-altitude environment.

## How the Mount Roraima Ascent Unfolds

### Stage One: Savanna, Rivers, and Base Camp

After arriving in [Caracas](/venezuela/place/caracas/), travelers head southeast. The mountain section begins near [San Francisco de Yuruani](/venezuela/place/san-francisco-de-yuruani/) and the Pemón village of Paraitepui. The trail crosses savanna and river valleys, with views of Mount Roraima and neighboring Kukenán Tepui.

Crossing the Tek and Kukenán rivers is among the demanding parts of the trek. During heavy rains, water levels rise and crossing conditions depend on the current. By evening, the group reaches a camp at the base of Roraima. The main ascent still lies ahead.

### Stage Two: Rocky Climb and Exploration of the Plateau

The trail climbs through forest, mosses, ferns, and rocky ground. A notable feature of the ascent is the “Two Tears” waterfall, which may soak the path after rain. On the plateau, the group camps in tents, including beneath natural rock overhangs.

A separate day is reserved for exploring the plateau. You can see rock formations, canyons, small pools, pinkish sand, and quartz crystals. Specialized high-altitude plants grow in nutrient-poor soils; some local species occur only on the tepuis. This part of the trek is valuable because travelers can explore the mountain close up rather than simply admire its outline from the plains.

### Stage Three: Descent and Return

After camping on the summit, travelers descend to the base and the Tek River, then return toward Paraitepui. Even on a familiar trail, these are full days of walking. On both itineraries, the core trek occupies the middle of the 12-day journey, with flights and river excursions following.

## What Makes Roraima's Nature Special?

Roraima is one of the tepuis, table mountains formed from the ancient rocks of the Guiana Highlands. In Canaima National Park, they create a characteristic landscape of immense rocky plateaus above forests and savannas, sheer cliffs, and waterfalls. Canaima has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1994.

The landscape changes repeatedly during the hike: open grasslands, riverbanks, dense forest, a rocky ascent, and finally the nearly treeless summit. **Climbing Roraima therefore has its own appeal even for travelers who have seen other South American mountains.** The experience lies in passing through varied natural zones and spending several days on a self-sufficient camping trek.

## When Is the Best Time to Plan the Trek?

Both itineraries note that **from June to December**, crossings of the Tek and Kukenán can be complicated by high water and strong currents. Mist and sudden weather changes are possible on the upper plateau in different seasons, so choosing a departure date solely for the chance of sunshine would be misleading.

Consider the state of the river crossings, cooler nights, rainfall, and the possibility of carrying out the subsequent river trip in Canaima. These factors need to be assessed for the entire itinerary, including transfers and the charter between Puerto Ordaz and Canaima. Exact departure dates and conditions are stated on each current tour page.

## Who Is the Trek For, and How Should You Prepare?

Roraima suits people comfortable with several consecutive days of hiking, camping, and changeable weather. Familiarity with walking on uneven ground matters more than a desire to see an unusual mountain from a viewpoint.

Broken-in trekking boots, rain protection, a warm layer for overnight stays, and a way to keep spare clothes dry are essential. Prepare for river crossings and steep trail sections. Check separately whether tents, mattresses, sleeping bags, and porter services are rented or provided: **they are not automatically included in both tours**. Equipment and guiding may differ.
